title: Too Many Young Men Don’t Know How to Be a Gentleman
author: Leonard Sax
summary: Family physician Leonard Sax uses the Cornell fraternity lawsuit as a prompt to ask a deeper question than the criticism of prosecutors and the university. He asks how Ivy League men could see nothing wrong in taking sexual advantage of an intoxicated woman. In school visits he shows a scene from Superbad and asks whether students know the rule that a gentleman does not take advantage of a drunk woman, and only three or four of 400 raise a hand. He argues that adults have failed to teach the rule and that boys are immersed in violent pornography and a culture that sends the opposite message. Citing data on porn exposure, coercive sex and young women's declining interest in dating men, he says boys must be taught to govern themselves and channel desire into romance. His call is to teach boys the rules with authority and to inspire them to be better men.
points: Sax contends that the question after the Cornell case is not only about prosecution but about what boys were never taught.
Students rarely know the old rule that a gentleman does not take advantage of a woman who is drunk or vulnerable.
He ties moral failure to widespread, increasingly violent pornography and to a culture that teaches the opposite.
Many young women say they want kind men who protect them, yet interest in dating men has fallen.
Adults, including parents and school leaders, should teach the word and ideal of the gentleman with authority.
quotes: I explain to the students that Evan is trying to obey a rule from an earlier era, namely: A gentleman does not take advantage of a woman when she is drunk.
Then I say, “Raise your hand if you have ever heard that rule.” In an auditorium of 400 students, typically only about three or four students will raise their hand.
I would argue that these men didn’t know because we, as adults, have failed to teach them. And because they are immersed in a toxic culture that sends a very different message.
One of the most toxic messages comes from widespread pornography. Pornography today is more pervasive—and more violent.
For a boy to become a good man, he must be taught how to govern himself—how to channel his sexual desire into romance rather than into violence. In short, how to be a gentleman.
In fact, I find that many school leaders and even many parents I talk to today are uncomfortable with the word “gentleman.” Perhaps the word sounds old-fashioned.
We need to inspire our boys to be better men. That’s what those Cornell men needed and apparently never received.
